configuration.note: Bounds, opacity and the data URI are checked in validateWorkflow; the georeference's CORRECTNESS is not checkable here and is recorded as not established in experiment 143.

ports.note: The `ground` port type was added to the closed union for this widget, which is a base-contract change made deliberately under D4. A plate must not reach clip_raster or sample_raster: its pixels are ink, and sampling them returns the colour of a line. The port type makes that connection impossible rather than reporting it after it is made.

ontology.note: GAP, meaning no alignment to an external cartographic vocabulary -- not meaning the terms are undeclared. fw:MapImageInput and fw:MapImage are declared in ontology/runtime.ttl with their properties. The receipt asserts the digest, the pixel dimensions, the four bounds, the ground resolution in metres and `fw:layerRole "context"`, which is the limit stated where a reader meets the layer rather than only in a document.

changes.description: A crosshair at the centre of the image pane, and Zoom in and Zoom out keep what is under it in place; the pane keeps its place when a click redraws the dialog (the practitioner, 2026-11-10: "once zoomed in it's hard to figure out where the glowing circle is"). A worked example's cue is shown only on the example's own image, whose size it states; on another image the dialog says so and shows none.

evidence.note: Nine unit tests over the world-file reader, the extent it derives, the ground resolution and each refusal: a rotated world file, a flipped image, crossed corners, corners outside the world, and a projection that sends the plate nowhere finite. Checked against the example's own geo/map2.jgw byte for byte. That the georeference is CORRECT. The control points were placed by a reader of the plate and this draws what they recorded; an alignment error looks exactly like a correct placement. Measuring the residual against modern boundaries is what would close it. That a reader understands what a historical wash means. The plate's own legend and the example's prose do that work. That 1002x788 over South London, about 40 m per pixel, is enough for anything but ground. There is nothing here for a lab check to recompute -- placing an image where its georeference says has no second implementation that could disagree -- so widgets/check-coverage.json records `none` with that reason rather than claiming parity this project's arithmetic would be agreeing with itself about. 0.2.0: tests/georeference.test.mjs (4: an exact affine recovered; too few or collinear points refused; South London's four points refitted, north-south agreeing with the hand fit and east-west differing by the direction of the fit; a turned image drawn through a matrix) and tests/map-image.test.mjs. 0.3.0: tests/georeference.test.mjs (5: a click on a guide feature, on each pane, within its radius) and tests/georeference-dialog.browser.mjs (the feature and its reason named, the pulse on both panes at 2.4 s, a click on the feature said, nothing filled, the pulse off on request and still under reduced motion). 0.4.0: tests/georeference.test.mjs (6: the fit's scale and turn recovered, the error history, a pair 30 m off measured against the others) and tests/hagelloch-sheet-example.browser.mjs (the live check, the cursor distance, and the preview with its slider and four pairs drawn twice). 0.4.1: tests/georeference-dialog.browser.mjs (a cleared field reads as not clicked yet). 0.5.0: tests/hagelloch-sheet-example.browser.mjs (the cue held under the crosshair through three zooms and a redraw) and tests/georeference-dialog.browser.mjs (no cue on another image).
